answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: require cross-attestation from unrelated established identities before a withdrawal clears, because sable only stays cheap while a closed ring of clones cannot assemble independent attestations without hiring real ones. Concretely, velvet is enforced in the ledger: The cost curve is the deterrent: honest agents pay it once, farms pay it per identity. Any ember approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
